settings.editor:
Interior painting starts long before the first coat. Furniture and floors are covered and protected. Walls and ceilings are inspected, and nail holes and cracks are filled and repaired. Baseboards, windows and frames are taped and caulked.

We prime new drywall and texture, then apply two coats of high-quality paint. In our dry mountain climate, a single coat can crack, so two coats is our standard.

settings.html:
How long does an interior painting project take?
It depends on the size of the space, ceiling heights and how much repair is needed. A single room is often a day or two, and a whole home can take a few weeks. Your written estimate includes a schedule.
Do we need to move out while you paint?
Usually not. We work room by room, keep paths clear and clean up at the end of every day. We use low-odor paints, and for whole-home projects some clients choose to be away for a few days.
Do you move the furniture?
Yes. We move and cover furniture and put it back when we're done. We ask you to put away small valuables, artwork and anything fragile before we start.
Can you help us choose colors?
Yes. We can talk through options with you and put samples on your walls, so you see them in your own light before you decide.
What paint do you use?
Premium coatings from manufacturers including Sherwin-Williams and Benjamin Moore, chosen for the surface and the room. Two full coats is our standard.
Is the work guaranteed?
Yes. Our work is backed by a two-year written warranty.
Do you offer financing?
Yes. We offer financing through Hearth. See financing options.
When is the best time for interior painting?
Any time of year works, but winter is ideal: schedules are flexible and many homes are quiet. Book between November 1 and March 31 and receive 10% off interior projects.
